correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary singular cubical 3-map in a finite triangle-free graph, each boundary 4-walk is an embedded square or a backtracking-null walk. Filling its six faces in the rigid-square two-complex gives a continuous S^2-map. As pi_2(X)=0, its H_2 class vanishes, and dimension(X)<=2 ensures the oriented square chain is zero, not merely homologous to zero. A face with coefficient ±1 at a chosen square therefore must have a second face supported on that square, giving 2-monophobicity. The published Jamil-Behrens integral comparison yields H_2^cub=H_2(X). For m,n>=5, the only squares in C_m □ C_n are product plaquettes, no 3-cells occur and X is the torus; connected dual-face adjacency makes H_2(X;Z)=Z. Independent finite tests replayed the fixed-face singular cube argument on C5 □ C5 (49 maps, no violations) and found an explicit length-4-factor violation on C4 □ C5 (52 maps, one violation), a boundary test not an infinite proof.
